A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AndroidWorld and M3A. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, code listings and appendices support comparison; relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent and human success rates in Table 3, human task characterizations in Figure 2, and task-parameter robustness results in Figure 3.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports development bug findings and human failure observations in Appendix C.4.

M1.justification: The M3A action/reflection procedure, text and SoM inputs, Android action interface, parameterized tasks and system-state rewards remain unchanged. The added SeeAct prompt and SMS teardown pseudocode document components already described in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 116 AndroidWorld tasks across 20 apps and evaluate the same 62-task MobileMiniWoB++ subset. The five tasks newly detailed in Table 5 already appear in v1's robustness experiment; additional related-work benchmarks are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the same human comparator, four M3A input/model configurations and Android-adapted SeeAct baseline. Appendix D.5 supplies SeeAct implementation details without establishing a changed comparator. Expanded Table 1 entries concern research positioning.

E3.justification: The evaluation retains seed 30, task-specific step budgets, GPT-4 Turbo and Gemini 1.5 Pro, and the same benchmark subsets. Appendix C.4 newly documents the existing human evaluation, including one attempt per participant per task, without reporting a protocol revision.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 adds a brief human-error analysis covering misunderstandings, input mistakes and unfamiliar interfaces. The five-task seed robustness analysis and four illustrated M3A error categories remain unchanged; the error figures are reordered.

E5.justification: v1 already displays error bars and p < 0.05 markers in Figure 3. v3 explicitly identifies the intervals as 95% Wilson binomial proportion confidence intervals. This clarifies uncertainty reporting without establishing additional runs or a new significance test.

E6.justification: All Table 3 scores and Figure 3 success rates are retained. v3 newly reports over 30 development bugs found and resolved, plus human failure patterns, in Appendix C.4. It omits v1's qualitative statement that agents perform better on data-editing than data-entry tasks.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theorems, proofs or substantive formal derivations. Expanded task pseudocode and identification of the confidence-interval method introduce no new mathematical definition or theoretical argument.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the broad claim that multimodal perception significantly improves performance with a qualified statement that it helps in some cases but generally does not outperform text-only input. It also narrows the robustness summary toward intent-parameter variation. The benchmark contribution and headline 30.6% success rate remain.

C2.justification: Appendix C.4 newly explains imperfect human performance through task misunderstandings, minor input errors and unfamiliar interfaces under a single-attempt procedure. v3 omits v1's explicit explanation that longer workflows accumulate more mistakes. The main open-source-app limitations and agent failure interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands reproducibility documentation: the full adapted SeeAct prompt in Appendix D.5, six annotators and two human evaluators with procedural details in C.4, initialization and validation descriptions for five existing robustness tasks in Table 5, and explicit SMS teardown pseudocode. These additions document existing work rather than demonstrate changed experiments.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands benchmark positioning with WorkArena, WindowsAgentArena, Mobile-Env, AndroidControl, AndroidArena and LlamaTouch, among other additions. It adds an explicit distinction from AndroidEnv's instrumented rewards. The B-MoCA comparison changes from 31 tasks across 12 apps to its reported experimental coverage of six tasks across four apps.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten, and the conclusion is substantially compressed. Experimental interpretation receives a separate Analysis subsection, error discussions are reordered, and the appendices gain ethical considerations, human-evaluation documentation and SeeAct details.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 5 expand, with Table 5 growing from two examples to seven. Figure 3 extends its vertical axis to 100% and revises its caption. Figures 6 and 7 exchange order, and several displays change size or placement; the overall visual format and remaining figure content are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves clarity and auditability by correcting the introduction's overgeneralized multimodality claim, identifying Figure 3's confidence intervals, and documenting human evaluation and the SeeAct prompt. Expanded related work clarifies the benchmark's contribution. A new Table 5 inconsistency describes deletion during initialization of ExpenseAddSingle despite its addition goal. Overall, the documentation gains outweigh this limited defect, while experimental coverage and principal results remain unchanged.
